# Options

<!-- Generated by internal/docsgen. Do not edit; run `go generate ./...`. -->

This has two halves.

**[imapsync options](#imapsync-options)** lists every option imapsync 2.x accepts
and what `imapsync-go compat` does with it. It is generated from the same table
the shim executes, so it describes what the tool does rather than what anyone
remembers it doing.

**[Native reference](#native-reference)** is the help for `imapsync-go`'s own
commands, which are what `imapsync-go sync` takes directly.

## imapsync options

218 options: 39 translate to a native flag, 16 build an endpoint URL, 70 are accepted and do nothing, and 93 are refused.

A **refused** option stops the run rather than being quietly dropped: an
option that changes which messages move, or where they land, is not something to
guess about. An **ignored** one is accepted because it asks for what already
happens here.

## Native reference

Generated from the commands' own `--help`.

### `imapsync-go`

```
Concurrent IMAP account synchronisation

Usage:
  imapsync-go [command]

Available Commands:
  compat      Run a sync from an imapsync command line
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  dedup       Remove messages a destination account holds more than once
  help        Help about any command
  oauth       Obtain and store OAuth credentials
  probe       Inspect an IMAP server's capabilities, folders and connection ceiling
  sync        Copy messages from one IMAP account to another

Flags:
  -h, --help               help for imapsync-go
      --log-json           force JSON logs (default: JSON when stderr is not a terminal)
      --log-level string   log level: debug, info, warn or error (default "info")
  -v, --version            version for imapsync-go

Use "imapsync-go [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### `imapsync-go sync`

```
Sync copies every message the destination does not already hold.

It is safe to interrupt and re-run. Progress is recorded in a state database as
the copy proceeds, and a message whose append was in flight when the process
stopped is searched for on the destination before it is copied again.

Copying runs over several connections at once, across folders and within a
single large one. Servers differ enormously in how many connections they will
tolerate, so raise --source-connections and --dest-connections gradually and
watch for authentication failures.

Usage:
  imapsync-go sync [flags]

Examples:
  # Straight from flags
  imapsync-go sync \
      --source-url imaps://you@imap.mail.me.com --source-password-env ICLOUD_APP_PW \
      --dest-url imaps://you@mox.example.net   --dest-password-keychain mox-imap

  # See what would happen without writing anything
  imapsync-go sync --config imapsync.yaml --pair icloud-to-mox --dry-run

  # One folder only, mapped somewhere specific
  imapsync-go sync --config imapsync.yaml --folder INBOX --map 'INBOX=Archive/Old'

Flags:
      --age-basis string                            which date --max-age and --min-age measure from: "sent" (the Date: header) or "internal" (arrival in the mailbox) (default "sent")
      --automap                                     map special folders such as Sent and Trash onto the destination's own names (default true)
      --config string                               path to a configuration file
      --delete2                                     delete destination messages whose source counterpart is gone
      --delete2-ceiling float                       refuse to delete more than this fraction of a folder's copied messages in one run (default 0.1)
      --delete2duplicates                           remove messages the destination holds more than once, keeping one (implied by --delete2; give --delete2duplicates=false to decline)
      --dest-connections int                        connections to open to the destination; overrides the config's concurrency.dest (default 16)
      --dest-insecure                               skip TLS certificate verification for the destination, for example a self-signed server on your own network
      --dest-oauth-cmd string                       command printing an OAuth access token for the destination
      --dest-oauth-file string                      file holding an OAuth access token for the destination
      --dest-oauth-refresh-env oauth login          environment variable holding the destination OAuth credential written by oauth login
      --dest-oauth-refresh-file oauth login         file holding the destination OAuth credential written by oauth login
      --dest-oauth-refresh-keychain oauth login     macOS keychain service name holding the destination OAuth credential written by oauth login
      --dest-password-env string                    environment variable holding the destination password
      --dest-password-file string                   file holding the destination password
      --dest-password-keychain string               macOS keychain service name holding the destination password
      --dest-search string                          consider only destination messages matching this IMAP SEARCH for deletion by --delete2
      --dest-url string                             destination endpoint URL
      --dial-timeout duration                       connection establishment timeout (default 30s)
      --dry-run                                     report what would be copied without writing anything
      --exclude strings                             skip source folders matching this regular expression (repeatable)
      --folder strings                              copy only these source folders, by exact name (repeatable)
      --force                                       carry out deletions the ceiling would otherwise refuse
      --full                                        examine every folder, even ones the server says have not changed
  -h, --help                                        help for sync
      --include strings                             copy only source folders matching this regular expression (repeatable)
      --include-virtual                             copy virtual mailboxes such as Gmail's All Mail, which duplicate the account
      --map stringArray                             explicit folder mapping as source=dest (repeatable)
      --max-age string                              skip messages older than this, for example 30d
      --max-bytes-per-second string                 hold the whole run to this much message data per second, for example 2MiB; a message is counted once and crosses the wire twice, so expect about double this in network traffic
      --max-messages-per-second float               hold the whole run to this many messages per second whatever their size; fractions are allowed
      --max-size string                             skip messages this large or larger, for example 25MiB
      --memory-limit string                         how much message data may be held in memory at once; overrides the config's concurrency.max_inflight (default "256MiB")
      --min-age string                              skip messages newer than this
      --min-size string                             skip messages this small or smaller
      --noresyncflags                               leave flags on already-copied messages alone
      --pair string                                 pair name within the configuration file
      --progress-interval duration                  how often to report what the sync has done so far; 0 to keep quiet (default 30s)
      --resyncflags                                 bring flags on already-copied messages back into line with the source (default true)
      --source-connections int                      connections to open to the source; overrides the config's concurrency.source (default 16)
      --source-insecure                             skip TLS certificate verification for the source (test use only)
      --source-oauth-cmd string                     command printing an OAuth access token for the source, re-run when the server refuses the one held
      --source-oauth-file string                    file holding an OAuth access token for the source, re-read when the server refuses the one held
      --source-oauth-refresh-env oauth login        environment variable holding the source OAuth credential written by oauth login
      --source-oauth-refresh-file oauth login       file holding the source OAuth credential written by oauth login
      --source-oauth-refresh-keychain oauth login   macOS keychain service name holding the source OAuth credential written by oauth login
      --source-password-env string                  environment variable holding the source password
      --source-password-file string                 file holding the source password
      --source-password-keychain string             macOS keychain service name holding the source password
      --source-search string                        copy only source messages matching this IMAP SEARCH, for example "UNSEEN SMALLER 100000"
      --source-url string                           source endpoint URL, for example imaps://user@host:993
      --state string                                path to the state database (default: per-user application state directory)
      --subfolder2 string                           nest the whole copied tree under this destination folder
      --subscribe                                   subscribe to destination folders as they are created, so clients show them (default true)
      --sync-duplicates                             copy a folder's repeated messages once each instead of once in total
      --trace                                       print the raw IMAP conversation to stderr, with credentials redacted
      --verify-dest                                 check the destination still holds the copies the state database recorded, and copy back any it does not (default true)

Global Flags:
      --log-json           force JSON logs (default: JSON when stderr is not a terminal)
      --log-level string   log level: debug, info, warn or error (default "info")
```

### `imapsync-go compat`

```
Compat reads imapsync's options and runs the equivalent sync.

It is meant for a command line that already works. Link this binary as
"imapsync" and it will behave as though it had been asked for compat, so an
existing cron line needs no editing at all:

    ln -s imapsync-go imapsync

Every option is answered. Most are translated, some are accepted and reported
as having done nothing, and the rest are refused with the reason and, where
there is one, the native flag to use instead. Nothing is dropped in silence: a
flag that changes which messages move, or what becomes of the ones that do not,
stops the run rather than being quietly forgotten.

The translation is printed before it runs, so it can be read, corrected, and
eventually pasted into the cron line in place of the imapsync one. A password
given as --password1 is passed through the environment rather than on the
command line, so the printed translation is safe to keep.

Usage:
  imapsync-go compat [imapsync options] [flags]

Examples:
  # As imapsync would have been called
  imapsync-go compat --host1 imap.mail.me.com --user1 you@example.com --password1 secret --ssl1 \
                     --host2 mox.example.net  --user2 you           --password2 other  --ssl2

  # See what it becomes without doing anything
  imapsync-go compat --dry --host1 ... --host2 ...

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for compat

Global Flags:
      --log-json           force JSON logs (default: JSON when stderr is not a terminal)
      --log-level string   log level: debug, info, warn or error (default "info")
```

### `imapsync-go probe`

```
Probe connects to an IMAP endpoint and reports what it can support:
negotiated capabilities, namespace and hierarchy delimiter, the folder list with
SPECIAL-USE attributes, and optionally the practical simultaneous connection
limit.

The connection ceiling is measured by opening connections until the server
refuses. It is off by default because it is intrusive; enable it with
--max-connections.

Usage:
  imapsync-go probe [flags]

Examples:
  # Straight from flags, no config file needed
  imapsync-go probe --url imaps://you@imap.mail.me.com --password-env ICLOUD_APP_PW

  # Find the practical connection limit and per-folder counts
  imapsync-go probe --url imaps://you@mox.example.net --password-keychain mox-imap \
      --max-connections 16 --status

  # From a config file
  imapsync-go probe --config imapsync.yaml --pair icloud-to-mox --side both

Flags:
      --config string                        path to a configuration file
      --dial-timeout duration                connection establishment timeout (default 30s)
  -h, --help                                 help for probe
      --insecure                             skip TLS certificate verification (test use only)
      --json                                 emit the report as JSON
      --max-connections int                  measure the connection ceiling, opening at most this many connections (0 disables)
      --oauth-cmd string                     command printing an OAuth access token, for a server that no longer accepts passwords
      --oauth-file string                    file holding an OAuth access token
      --oauth-refresh-env oauth login        environment variable holding the OAuth credential written by oauth login
      --oauth-refresh-file oauth login       file holding the OAuth credential written by oauth login
      --oauth-refresh-keychain oauth login   macOS keychain service name holding the OAuth credential written by oauth login
      --pair string                          pair name within the configuration file
      --password-env string                  environment variable holding the password
      --password-file string                 file holding the password
      --password-keychain string             macOS keychain service name holding the password
      --side string                          which endpoint of the pair to probe: source, dest or both (default "both")
      --status                               include per-folder message counts and UIDVALIDITY
      --trace                                print the raw IMAP conversation to stderr, with credentials redacted
      --url string                           endpoint URL, for example imaps://user@host:993

Global Flags:
      --log-json           force JSON logs (default: JSON when stderr is not a terminal)
      --log-level string   log level: debug, info, warn or error (default "info")
```

### `imapsync-go oauth`

```
Obtain and store OAuth credentials.

Providers that speak XOAUTH2 hand out access tokens that expire within the
hour, which is shorter than a migration. `oauth login` walks the consent
flow once and stores the long-lived half, so a sync can mint access tokens
for itself as it runs.

Usage:
  imapsync-go oauth [command]

Available Commands:
  login       Consent once and store a refresh credential

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for oauth

Global Flags:
      --log-json           force JSON logs (default: JSON when stderr is not a terminal)
      --log-level string   log level: debug, info, warn or error (default "info")

Use "imapsync-go oauth [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### `imapsync-go oauth login`

```
Consent once in a browser and store the resulting refresh credential.

The credential is one JSON document. Give it to a sync with
--source-oauth-refresh-file, --source-oauth-refresh-keychain or
--source-oauth-refresh-env, or the matching --dest- flags, or name it
under `oauth.refresh` in a configuration file.

You need an OAuth client of your own. Neither provider allows a shared
one: Google's mail scope is restricted and needs verification plus an
annual security assessment, and Microsoft's IMAP scope needs tenant
admin consent whoever asks. Register a desktop or native client, allow
the redirect http://localhost, and pass its details here.

Usage:
  imapsync-go oauth login [flags]

Examples:
  # Gmail, from the JSON the Google console hands you
  imapsync-go oauth login --client-file client_secret.json \
      --scope https://mail.google.com/ --out gmail.oauth.json

  # Exchange Online, storing the result in the macOS keychain
  imapsync-go oauth login \
      --client-id $APP_ID \
      --auth-url https://login.microsoftonline.com/$TENANT/oauth2/v2.0/authorize \
      --token-url https://login.microsoftonline.com/$TENANT/oauth2/v2.0/token \
      --scope https://outlook.office365.com/IMAP.AccessAsUser.All \
      --scope offline_access \
      --keychain imapsync-work

Flags:
      --account string         mailbox to consent as, offered to the provider as a hint
      --auth-url string        provider authorization endpoint
      --client-file string     JSON client credential downloaded from the Google console
      --client-id string       OAuth client ID
      --client-secret string   OAuth client secret, if the provider issues one
  -h, --help                   help for login
      --keychain string        store the credential in the macOS keychain under this service name
      --no-open                print the URL instead of opening a browser
      --out string             write the credential to this file, created readable only by you
      --scope stringArray      scope to request, repeatable
      --stdout                 print the credential on standard output
      --timeout duration       how long to wait for consent (default 5m0s)
      --token-url string       provider token endpoint

Global Flags:
      --log-json           force JSON logs (default: JSON when stderr is not a terminal)
      --log-level string   log level: debug, info, warn or error (default "info")
```
